rationale: Screen-shot domain experiment. Measured 2026-09-29 with the deployed det2b head on 264 authentic, unmodified desktop web screenshots: 45.5% (91/200) and 48.4% (31/64) were flagged as manipulated at threshold 0.5, mean score ~0.48. The same model scored 0/2 on the two authentic LINE/screen captures (chatshot2, mean 0.71). The head has no usable representation of the screenshot/UI domain, and the training manifest contains no screenshot source at all. This block adds Det-Head/det-train-v4-webshot.csv (7,394 rows, all Det label 0) to the Train set and measures whether the screenshot false positives move. Block 2 is the control: the same architectures and seeds without the new data, so any difference is attributable to the added rows and not to run-to-run variance. The screenshot rows are all label 0 on purpose: a screenshot of a phishing site is still an unmodified image, and mapping the source phishing label to Det label 1 would train the head to flag untouched screenshots.

protocol.note: Screening only. The webshot rows are always included in the subsample so the comparison is against the previous run, which used the identical 25,000-row budget drawn from the base manifest alone. Screening Val accuracy is not comparable to full-data Val accuracy and never accepts a candidate; the external diagnostics are the gate.

candidates.name: w00_control_no_webshot
candidates.note: Control. Reproduces s00_control_patch_attention_8x8, which scored camera9 18.18%, chatshot2 0/2, pilot11 45.45%, testcases 84.24% under the old camera11 split. Under the camera9/chatshot2 split its numbers will differ slightly, so this run is the reference rather than the archived s00 row.

candidates.note: Primary test: does adding 7,394 authentic screenshot rows change the screenshot false positives?
